verified_by_source.finding: start writes desired running; begin_stop writes desired draining with installation token and current logon session.
SUPERVISOR_PENDING without generation is handled; stop takes launch_exclusion, revalidates current identity and latches begin_stop even before process readiness.
Supervised child takes same launch_exclusion and returns before runtime when desired draining matches current logon.

conclusion: Remote stop must wait until auxiliary Job is empty; otherwise consumer could overwrite the stop latch. After Job0 this still does not prove Scheduler empty or physical service exit. Canonical normal stop applies the current same-logon fence, and separate task/PID-birth/exit checks remain mandatory before uninstall.
residual_limit: If Scheduler has accepted a start but ownership changes before stop, canonical stop may return INSTANCE_CHANGED or another uncertainty. The one-shot wrapper does not replay; no shutdown or native exit success is inferred. Helper dispatch is conservatively reserved before its monitor preflight, so refusal before thread start can retain UNKNOWN and requires read-only reconciliation.
